_README: STARTER VALUES. Every entry below is an order-of-magnitude-correct placeholder
drawn from general pharmacology knowledge, NOT from a checked primary source.
verified=false means: do not put this number in front of a user, and do not
cite it in a write-up, until someone has opened the reference and confirmed it.
The spec requires a citation per parameter set. Replace `source` with a real
reference and flip `verified` to true, one substance at a time.
common_side_effects: a short local fallback list for the symptom check, used only when openFDA has no label.
It is from general knowledge, not a cited source, and is unverified like everything else here.

threshold_explanation: why the threshold_24h_mg limit matters, shown as 'Why this matters' next to an alert. Null unless the limit's clinical consequence is documented; conservative and factual only -- no frequency, mortality, or comparison claims unless cited. Unverified like everything else here.

Units: half_life_hours h | vd_l_per_kg L/kg | ka_per_hour 1/h | threshold_24h_mg, threshold_single_mg mg | threshold_concentration_mg_per_l mg/L (null unless a published concentration is cited; never derived from a dose threshold)

substances.name: Caffeine
substances.threshold_explanation: Above 400 mg/day, caffeine is associated with anxiety, insomnia, rapid heartbeat, and digestive issues. Individual sensitivity varies widely.

substances.name: Acetaminophen
substances.threshold_explanation: The 4000 mg daily limit is set by the FDA to prevent liver damage. Exceeding it repeatedly can cause acute liver failure. Risk increases with alcohol use or liver impairment.
substances.notes: Canonical duplication case. Threshold drops with hepatic impairment or chronic alcohol use.

substances.name: Ibuprofen
substances.threshold_explanation: The 1200 mg OTC daily limit reduces the risk of stomach bleeding, kidney problems, and cardiovascular events. Higher doses are sometimes prescribed under supervision.
substances.notes: 1200 mg is the OTC ceiling; prescription ceiling is higher. Registry should eventually carry both.

substances.name: Aspirin
substances.notes: Hydrolysed to salicylate, which has saturable elimination. The engine refuses to curve this; show a warning instead.

substances.name: Diphenhydramine
substances.threshold_explanation: Exceeding 300 mg in 24 hours increases risk of seizures, hallucinations, and cardiac arrhythmia. Older adults are more sensitive.
substances.notes: Second duplication case: sleep aids and cold medicines both carry it.

substances.name: Loratadine
substances.notes: Active metabolite desloratadine has a longer half-life; single-parent modelling understates duration.

substances.name: Cetirizine
substances.notes: Good renal-adjustment demo: largely excreted unchanged.

substances.name: Metformin
substances.notes: The strongest case for Cockcroft-Gault in the registry.

substances.name: Azithromycin
substances.notes: Very long half-life; useful as an accumulation demo over a 5-day course.

substances.name: Warfarin
substances.notes: Dosing is INR-driven, not concentration-driven. No threshold is meaningful. The UI must not imply the curve tells you whether a dose is safe.

substances.name: Omeprazole
substances.notes: Plasma half-life is short but the pharmacodynamic effect long outlasts it. Concentration curve is a poor proxy for effect here.

substances.name: Melatonin
substances.notes: Supplement; bioavailability is highly variable between people and products.

substances.name: Nicotine
substances.notes: Bioavailability differs enormously by route. One value across gum, patch and inhalation is wrong; split into route-specific entries in Phase 2.

substances.name: Alcohol (ethanol)
substances.notes: Zero-order elimination, roughly a fixed amount per hour regardless of concentration. The first-order engine cannot model it and raises UnsupportedKinetics. Either implement Widmark separately or drop alcohol from v1.

substances.name: Minoxidil (topical)
substances.notes: Transdermal absorption is low but nonzero and highly variable with scalp condition. This is the substance the overview leans on rhetorically, so its numbers need real sourcing before it appears in any demo.

substances.name: Doxylamine
substances.notes: Sleep-aid label max is 25 mg/24h; also present at low dose in NyQuil-type combination products, another duplication case alongside diphenhydramine.

substances.name: Phenylephrine
substances.notes: Oral bioavailability is low and disputed (extensive first-pass metabolism); the FDA's 2023 advisory review questioned its OTC efficacy at labelled doses. Population value here is a rough placeholder, not a settled number.

substances.name: Guaifenesin
substances.notes: Immediate-release OTC ceiling; extended-release products dose differently (up to 1200 mg per dose) and aren't distinguished here yet.

substances.name: Famotidine
substances.notes: OTC (Pepcid AC) label ceiling; prescription dosing is higher and not modelled here. Largely renally excreted, another Cockcroft-Gault candidate.
